name: Hepatocellular (liver) cancer
theme: the two-disease problem · the IO-doublet era

meta.title: Hepatocellular carcinoma in silico decision trainer
meta.population: Adults with HCC - THE TWO-DISEASE PROBLEM as the spec's spine: nearly every patient has two lethal conditions at once (a cancer and the cirrhotic liver it grew in), so every decision passes TWO gates - cancer extent (BCLC) and liver function (Child-Pugh) - and the trainer enforces both. A Child-Pugh C liver can make an early cancer untreatable by anything except the one therapy that cures both diseases at once (transplantation); a Child-Pugh A liver opens the full menu. The liver gate is this row's new pattern: a readiness gate that is not about the tumor at all.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the disease where the liver votes on every decision. THE LIVER GATE is the architecture: extent (BCLC) and liver function (Child-Pugh) are co-equal readiness gates - the menu refuses to rank until both report, because the same tumor is curable in a Child-Pugh A liver and a hospice conversation in a C. THE 1L TRIPLE MENU carries the registry's no-head-to-head discipline at full strength: three approved doublets (atezolizumab-bevacizumab per IMbrave150, verified 19.2 vs 13.4, with THE ENDOSCOPY-BEFORE-ANTIBODY artifact - a required EGD and treated varice…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: BCLC staging (2022 update verified; a 2026 refresh exists and is noted) as the extent axis; Child-Pugh (ALBI as the granular companion) as the LIVER-FUNCTION CO-GATE; Milan criteria for transplant candidacy (single <=5 cm or <=3 nodules each <=3 cm - the verified founding receipt); AFP >= 400 as the one proven biomarker door (REACH-2); NCCN Hepatocellular Carcinoma (split from Hepatobiliary since 2023; v1.2026 secondhand - 403)
meta.response: RECIST 1.1 (mRECIST where locoregional); the surveillance receipt is randomized and verified (ultrasound + AFP q6mo cut HCC mortality 37% in the Shanghai RCT) - surveillance of the cirrhotic liver is itself an evidence-based intervention, and after curative-intent treatment it is THE standard (the adjuvant chapter's tombstones say why)

Patient.label: Age

Patient.helpPatient: The health of the liver usually matters more than the birthday here.

Patient.label: Performance status (ECOG)
Patient.help: In HCC the performance score and the liver score entangle - decompensation masquerades as frailty.
Patient.helpPatient: Feeling weak here is often the liver, not the cancer - and liver care can turn it around.

The two diseases.label: Liver function (Child-Pugh - THE LIVER GATE)
The two diseases.help: THE LIVER GATE - this row's new pattern: a readiness gate that is not about the tumor. Every phase 3 receipt in advanced HCC enrolled Child-Pugh A; class B is the excluded-population honesty (its doo…
The two diseases.helpPatient: The liver's own health score decides as much as the cancer's stage - it is checked first, and re-checked at every visit.

The two diseases.label: Extent (BCLC)
The two diseases.help: BCLC is the extent axis (2022 receipt verified; a 2026 refresh exists and is noted) - and it only means anything WITH the liver gate: stage and score gate together.
The two diseases.helpPatient: Where the cancer stands is half the answer - the liver's score is the other half, and the plan needs both.

The two diseases.label: Within Milan criteria
The two diseases.help: Three measurements that decide transplant candidacy (verified founding receipt, NEJM 1996) - the only door that treats both diseases at once. Downstaging into Milan is real (ImmunoXXL's European rece…
The two diseases.helpPatient: A short list of size rules decides whether a liver transplant - which cures both the cancer and the cirrhosis - is on the table.

Later-line routing.label: AFP >= 400 ng/mL
Later-line routing.help: The one proven biomarker door in HCC: REACH-2 enrolled AFP>=400 only (after REACH overall missed) and won OS there - the threshold is the ticket, exactly.
Later-line routing.helpPatient: One blood-test threshold opens one specific later-line drug - because that is exactly who its trial helped.

Later-line routing.label: Prior checkpoint-inhibitor exposure
Later-line routing.help: IMbrave251 (negative, final) proved the post-IO gap open: continuing atezolizumab beyond progression adds nothing, and no 2L regimen has a receipt in the post-doublet population - the TKI default is…
Later-line routing.helpPatient: For disease that grew through a first-line combination, the honest truth is that the next step's proof is borrowed from an older era - and one new trial door is asking the modern question.

On treatment.label: Response read
On treatment.help: Progression has TWO currencies here: the tumor can grow, or the liver can decompensate with no tumor growth at all - and either closes menus. The checkpoint reads both.
On treatment.helpPatient: Follow-up watches two things at once: the cancer on scans, and the liver's own health - a change in either redirects the plan.

Newly diagnosed.name: Resection or ablation (BCLC 0/A + Child-Pugh A) - then surveillance, not adjuvant
Newly diagnosed.guideline: the BCLC 0/A CP-A standard (BCLC verified; NCCN secondhand); adjuvant NOTHING - three trials say so
Newly diagnosed.evidence: guideline-grade composite (flagged headline); the adjuvant tombstones verified beneath
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: procedure-scale; the liver's reserve is the real budget
Newly diagnosed.patient: For small cancers in a still-strong liver: surgery or needle-based heat treatment, given to cure - followed by careful watching every six months, because the add-on therapies were properly tested and did not help.

Newly diagnosed.name: Liver transplantation within Milan (the two-disease cure)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: the founding cohort verified (PMID-matched); the 4-yr figure flagged memory-grade
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the transplant ledger - surgery, immunosuppression for life - bought against curing BOTH diseases
Newly diagnosed.patient: For cancers within strict size rules: a new liver - the one treatment that cures the cancer and the cirrhosis at the same time, which is why it can remain possible even when the liver is too sick for anything else.

Newly diagnosed.name: TACE (BCLC B + Child-Pugh A - the standing standard; the combo wave broke)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: the BCLC-B CP-A standard on its own verified receipt; no combo is US-approved
Newly diagnosed.evidence: randomized (verified) - the wave's three PFS-only results carried at exact currency
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: post-embolization syndrome; the liver's reserve is the budget - decompensation risk is the real ceiling on repetition
Newly diagnosed.patient: For cancer confined to the liver but too large or numerous to cure: blocking the tumors' blood supply with targeted chemotherapy - the proven standard, with an honest note that adding immunotherapy to it was tested three times and did not extend life in the analyses US regulators require.

Newly diagnosed.name: Atezolizumab + bevacizumab (IMbrave150 - the EGD-gated door)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: 1L co-standard (verified receipt; the tie's honesty carried on all three cards)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - OS met (verified); display number is the property-enforced tie, flagged
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: immune ledger + bevacizumab's bleeding/pressure/proteinuria ledger - the EGD is the entry fee
Newly diagnosed.patient: One of three proven first-line combinations: immunotherapy plus a blood-vessel blocker - opened only after a camera check of the food-pipe veins, because that safety step was built into the proof itself.

Newly diagnosed.name: Tremelimumab + durvalumab, STRIDE (HIMALAYA - the varices-averse door)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: 1L co-standard (verified receipt; the tie's honesty carried)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - OS met with verified 5-year tail; display number is the tie, flagged
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the dual-immune ledger (the priming dose front-loads it) - no bleeding surcharge
Newly diagnosed.patient: One of three proven first-line combinations: two immunotherapies with no blood-vessel blocker - the natural door when food-pipe veins make bleeding a worry - with one in five patients alive at five years in its trial.

Newly diagnosed.name: Nivolumab + ipilimumab (CheckMate 9DW - the newest door, early-crossing honesty)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: 1L co-standard, newest (FDA 2025-04-11 verified; the tie's honesty carried)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - OS met vs the modern control (verified); display number is the tie, flagged; the early crossing said
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the strongest dual-immune ledger on the menu - and the early-months mortality signal is part of the honest picture
Newly diagnosed.patient: The newest of the three first-line combinations: two immunotherapies - with the deepest and longest responses in its trial, and an honest early-months caution that makes fitness part of the choice.

Newly diagnosed.name: Lenvatinib or sorafenib (REFLECT/SHARP - the IO-ineligible lane)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized x2 (SHARP verified; REFLECT noninferiority verified, medians flagged)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: hand-foot skin reaction, hypertension, fatigue - the TKI ledger
Newly diagnosed.patient: The tablet option: for people whose health history makes immunotherapy unsafe - proven, older, still real.

Newly diagnosed.name: Child-Pugh B advanced disease (the excluded population - honest thinness + named doors)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: no phase 3 receipt exists - cohort-grade + the named trial doors
Newly diagnosed.evidence: cohort/registry grade (flagged); the two CP-B trials ARE the honest offer
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: every ledger is heavier in a B liver - dose craft and low thresholds throughout
Newly diagnosed.patient: When the liver is moderately weakened, the honest truth is that the big trials excluded this exact situation - so the strongest options are two studies built specifically for it, with individualized treatment as the alternative.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care (and the Child-Pugh C honesty)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift; the default road for CP-C outside Milan - said plainly
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: none from therapy; hepatology comfort craft is the care
Newly diagnosed.patient: When the liver itself is failing, comfort-focused care is often the most honest medicine - with the transplant question asked first where the size rules allow it.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Cabozantinib / regorafenib 2L (the rack - with the post-IO extrapolation said)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: the 2L rack (verified receipts; post-IO use is extrapolated - said on the card)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized x2 (verified) - in the post-sorafenib population; post-doublet grade: extrapolation, flagged
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: the intensified TKI ledger - hand-foot, fatigue, weight loss; heavier in cirrhosis
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The proven next-line tablets - with an honest note: their proof comes from the era before today's first-line combinations, and the newest trials are asking whether something better exists for exactly this situation.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Ramucirumab (REACH-2 - the AFP >= 400 door, exactly)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized, biomarker-selected - OS met (HR verified; medians flagged)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: hypertension and proteinuria - the antibody's ledger, gentler than the rack's
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: For tumors with a very high AFP blood level: an antibody proven to extend life in exactly that group - the first liver-cancer drug whose proof was built around a blood test.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: teaching estimate (flagged); the saga and shelf dated
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Choosing comfort after the proven lines is a real road - and this card carries an unusual honesty: one effective drug combination has been rejected three times in the US for factory-inspection reasons, never for how well it works, and it still cannot be prescribed.

BCLC strategy for prognosis prediction and treatment recommendation: the 2022 update - J Hepatol 2022;76:681-693 (PMID 34801630, pubmed-url-match; the reply-correspondence at 35283212 is not the paper). Finn et al. IMbrave150: atezolizumab + bevacizumab vs sorafenib, 1L - NEJM 2020 (PMID 32402160, pubmed-url-match); updated median OS 19.2 vs 13.4 (J Hepatol 2022;76:862-873 - update paper's PMID UNMATCHED, cited by journal/pages: FLAG). THE ARTIFACT: EGD within 6 months + varices treated BEFORE therapy (bleeding 25% vs 17% any-grade; grade-5 upper-GI bleeds occurred). FDA 2020-05 (secondhand). The authors-reply correspondence at 32888463 is not the paper | PMID 32402160 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Abou-Alfa et al. HIMALAYA (STRIDE): tremelimumab x1 + durvalumab vs sorafenib - OS 16.4 vs 13.8 (HR 0.78, p=0.0035); durvalumab mono noninferior. NEJM Evidence 2022 (PMID 38319892, pubmed-url-match - late PMID is retro-indexing, not an error); 4-yr update (38382875, matched): 48-mo OS 25.2% vs 15.1%; 5-yr update (40222621, matched): HR 0.76, ~20% vs ~9% at 60 months. FDA 2022-10-21 (approval summary PMID 37676259, matched) | PMID 38319892 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

CheckMate 9DW: nivolumab + ipilimumab vs lenvatinib/sorafenib, 1L - OS 23.7 vs 20.6 (HR 0.79, p=0.018); ORR 36% vs 13%; DoR 30.4 vs 12.9 mo; THE EARLY CROSSING (excess deaths first ~6 months, then sustained separation) said out loud. Lancet 2025 (PMID 40349714, pubmed-url-match). FDA 2025-04-11 (verified via fda.gov). 4-yr follow-up sustains (ASCO GI 2026, secondhand). The 20.6 control is THE RISING BAR's third rung | PMID 40349714 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Llovet et al. SHARP: sorafenib vs placebo - OS 10.7 vs 7.9 (the founding receipt; the 7.9 is the rising bar's first rung). NEJM 2008 (PMID 18650514, pubmed-url-match; adjacent near-title review 19496710 and editorial 18817997 are NOT the primary) | PMID 18650514 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Kudo et al. REFLECT: lenvatinib noninferior to sorafenib, 1L (OS 13.6 vs 12.3 memory-grade, flagged; PFS/ORR superior verified-snippet). Lancet 2018 (PMID 29433850, pubmed-url-match) | PMID 29433850 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25
Bruix et al. RESORCE: regorafenib post-sorafenib - positive OS (10.6 vs 7.8 memory-grade). Lancet 2017 (PMID 27932229, pubmed-url-match) | PMID 27932229 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Abou-Alfa et al. CELESTIAL: cabozantinib post-sorafenib - OS 10.2 vs 8.0 (HR 0.76, p=0.005), PFS 5.2 vs 1.9 (verified). FDA 2019-01 (secondhand). NEJM 2018 (PMID 29972759, pubmed-url-match; the near-identical-title correspondence at 30285325 is NOT the paper - trap caught) | PMID 29972759 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Zhu et al. REACH-2: ramucirumab in AFP>=400 ONLY - OS HR 0.710 (p=0.0199): the FIRST positive biomarker-selected phase 3 in HCC (medians 8.5 vs 7.3 memory-grade, flagged); after REACH overall missed - the threshold IS the ticket. Lancet Oncol 2019 (PMID 30665869, pubmed-url-match; the comment at 30665868 is NOT the paper - trap caught) | PMID 30665869 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

IMbrave251: atezolizumab + TKI vs TKI alone AFTER atezo-bev progression - NEGATIVE at final (OS 14.6 vs 12.5, HR 0.88, p=0.2115; ASCO 2026 abstract - no PubMed record verified, secondhand): continuing checkpoint blockade beyond progression adds nothing; THE POST-IO GAP IS PROVEN OPEN and the 2L TKI default is EXTRAPOLATED - said on every card that uses it

Mazzaferro et al. Milan criteria: liver transplantation for small HCC in cirrhosis - single <=5 cm or <=3 nodules each <=3 cm; ~75% 4-yr OS (figure memory-grade, flagged); UNOS-adopted. NEJM 1996 (PMID 8594428, pubmed-url-match). The two-disease cure's founding receipt | PMID 8594428 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Vietti Violi et al. MWA vs RFA for small HCC - randomized phase 2, no significant difference in local progression (endpoint detail memory-grade). Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2018 (PMID 29503247, pubmed-url-match; the comment at 29503248 is NOT the paper - trap caught). SBRT: guideline-accepted alternative (lower confidence this sweep, flagged) | PMID 29503247 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

Llovet et al. Arterial embolisation/chemoembolisation vs symptomatic treatment - 2-yr survival 63% vs 27% (1-yr 82% vs 63%; death HR 0.47, p=0.025): the BCLC-B standard's verified receipt. Lancet 2002 (PMID 12049862, pubmed-url-match). The Lo 2002 companion (Hepatology 2002;35:1164-71) - PMID UNMATCHED after 3 attempts: FLAG, cited by journal/pages only | PMID 12049862 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

EMERALD-1: durvalumab +/- bevacizumab + TACE - PFS met (15.0 vs 8.2, HR 0.77 - medians memory-grade) but OS NEGATIVE at final (D+B HR 1.10); NOT approved. Lancet 2025 (PMID 39798579, pubmed-url-match). EMERALD-3 (STRIDE+lenva+TACE): PFS positive, OS NS (39.5 vs 34.7, HR 0.84, p=0.18 - ASCO 2026 LBA, secondhand). The wave broke on OS | PMID 39798579 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

LEAP-012: pembrolizumab + lenvatinib + TACE - PFS positive (HR 0.66, p=0.0002 verified via the matched 2026 companion paper PMID 41790022; the 2025 Lancet primary's PMID soft-flagged); CLOSED EARLY for OS futility in the US framework (Merck/Eisai) AND approved in China ON PFS (2025-06): ONE TRIAL, TWO REGULATORY VERDICTS - the currency lesson at the jurisdiction level. Not US-approved | REF FIX 2026-08-25: prior pointer 41790022 was a commentary; primary = Lancet 2025 PMID 39798578, abstract read firsthand

IMbrave050 - THE COMPLETED REVERSAL, both halves verified: HALF 1 - adjuvant atezo-bev vs surveillance, interim RFS HR 0.72 (p=0.012), primary endpoint MET (Lancet 2023, PMID 37871608, pubmed-url-match); HALF 2 - benefit NOT maintained at final ('updated results do not support use of atezo+bev in the adjuvant setting'; updated RFS HR 0.90 memory-grade; final pub J Hepatol 2026, PMID 41580093 title-matched). No FDA adjuvant approval. The near-identical-title item at 37484877 is commentary-class - NOT the primary. An interim is a promise; this one was withdrawn | PMID 37871608 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

KEYNOTE-937: adjuvant pembrolizumab after resection/ablation - NEGATIVE (mRFS 46.7 vs 45.5, HR 1.06, p=0.719 - ASCO GI 2026, secondhand). The adjuvant graveyard's second IO tombstone. EMERALD-2 (adjuvant durva+/-bev): accrual complete, readout imminent-but-absent; CheckMate 9DX (adjuvant nivo): OVERDUE AND SILENT - the loudest watch item

Bruix et al. STORM: adjuvant sorafenib after resection/ablation - NEGATIVE (RFS 33.3 vs 33.7 memory-grade). Lancet Oncol 2015 (PMID 26361969, pubmed-url-match; the 'wrong stage, wrong dose' editorial at 26433814 also matched). The adjuvant graveyard's founding tombstone | PMID 26361969 resolved + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-25

THE THREE-CRL SAGA (all secondhand, dated): camrelizumab + rivoceranib (CARES-310: OS 23.8 months verified-snippet; HR 0.62 memory-grade) - US rejections 2024-05-16 (camrelizumab site cGMP), 2025-03-20 (second CRL), 2026-07-10 (third CRL, rivoceranib site cGMP) - every one MANUFACTURING, never efficacy: an efficacy receipt without a license, carded nowhere. Tislelizumab: RATIONALE-301 noninferior (15.9 vs 14.1 verified-snippet) - NO US HCC approval found, not claimed. IMbrave152/SKYSCRAPER-14: TIGIT dead in HCC 1L (missed PFS, ESMO 2025)

Zhang et al. Randomized controlled trial of screening for hepatocellular carcinoma (Shanghai, n=18,816 HBV/chronic hepatitis): ultrasound + AFP q6mo - HCC mortality 83.2 vs 131.5 per 100,000 (rate ratio 0.63, CI 0.41-0.98); resection rate 46.5% vs 7.5%. THE SURVEILLANCE RECEIPT - randomized and verified. J Cancer Res Clin Oncol 2004 (PMID 15042359, pubmed-url-match)

Chang et al. Universal hepatitis B vaccination in Taiwan and childhood HCC - incidence 0.52 -> 0.13 per 100,000 (p<0.001): the registry's strongest prevention receipt. NEJM 1997 (PMID 9197213, pubmed-url-match - the sweep CAUGHT AND CORRECTED a wrong remembered PMID here: the discipline works); 20-year follow-up PMID 19759364 (matched). HBV antivirals reduce HCC (Liaw 2004 - NOT verified this sweep, soft-FLAG)

Ioannou et al. HCV eradication by DAAs reduces HCC risk ~71% (J Hepatol 2017, PMID 28887168, pubmed-url-match); residual risk persists >=10 years with cirrhosis/high FIB-4 - SURVEILLANCE CONTINUES AFTER CURE (PMID 31356807, matched). Kanwal 2017 corroborates (PMID unmatched - FLAG)

El-Jawahri A, LeBlanc T, VanDusen H, et al. Effect of Inpatient Palliative Care on Quality of Life 2 Weeks After Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA 2016;316(20):2094-2103 (PMID 27893130, NCT02207322) — abstract read firsthand 2026-09-10. POPULATION CAUTION, added at that read because the previous label named no population at all: this is a SINGLE-INSTITUTION randomized trial of 160 adults with HAEMATOLOGICAL malignancy hospitalized for autologous or allogeneic stem-cell transplantation, and its outcomes are quality of life, depression, anxiety, fatigue and symptom burden — it reports no survival and no adverse-event table. It is the factory's standing anchor for the PRINCIPLE that palliative care runs alongside active treatment rather than after it; it is not evidence in this tumour type and is not the source of any number on this card.

ARTEMIDE-HCC01 (NCT06921785): rilvegostomig (PD-1/TIGIT bispecific) + bev + treme vs rilve + bev vs atezo-bev, 1L uHCC CP-A (~1200 pts; started 2025-05; US sites incl. Medical College of Wisconsin) - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08-19, registry re-check due. The TIGIT question re-asked as a bispecific after the mAb failed

NCT06096779: atezolizumab +/- bevacizumab in Child-Pugh B7-B8, 1L (phase 2 multi-cohort, Genentech; US multi-site incl. UCSD) - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08-19 (registry status seen 2026-05), re-check due. The excluded population's sponsor-run door

NCT06526104: STRIDE (T300+D) in Child-Pugh B advanced HCC - phase 2 single-arm (UT Health San Antonio; started 2024-12) - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08-19 (seen 2026-01), re-check due. The IO-only CP-B door where varices worry

NCT05027425: durvalumab + tremelimumab BEFORE liver transplant (phase 2, n=30, Cincinnati + multicenter; primary endpoint = 30-day post-LT rejection) - recruiting claim NOT DATE-STAMPED: FLAG, registry re-check first. ImmunoXXL context (European atezo-bev downstaging -> LT: 2-yr RFS 90%, J Hepatol 2026 - PMID 41763363 noted, secondhand)
